question: Should OpenClaw permanently add optional `SandboxFsBridge.appendFile` to the public Plugin SDK and expose `write.append` only when the active backend implements that capability?
rationale: The patch is correct and well-proven, but it establishes a new public plugin/runtime contract and backend-dependent model tool surface; repository policy requires explicit owner intent for that API direction.

options.title: Sponsor capability-gated append
options.body: Accept the optional bridge method and conditional write schema as the supported contract, then reopen or resubmit this implementation for landing.

options.title: Keep append core-internal
options.body: Retain native append only on core-owned internal bridges and avoid expanding the public Plugin SDK contract.

options.title: Decline native append for now
options.body: Keep the existing overwrite-only public write contract until maintainers choose a broader file-concurrency product design.

recommendation.title: Sponsor capability-gated append
recommendation.body: Accept the optional bridge method and conditional write schema as the supported contract, then reopen or resubmit this implementation for landing.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history on the remote filesystem security boundary and adjacent public/runtime contracts.
